what: BridgeBio is a biotech that develops drugs for genetic diseases. Its first big product, acoramidis, treats a heart condition called ATTR cardiomyopathy, and it runs a pipeline of other genetic-disease programmes.
customers: Cardiologists and specialist centres prescribing to patients with inherited and rare conditions, paid for by insurers and national health systems.
money: the approved heart drug, launched in 2025
payments from partners on other programmes
moat: Patents and clinical data on drugs for diseases with few or no alternatives, in a field where a rival needs years of trials to arrive.
risks: Still loses money: about $592M of net loss on $945M of revenue
Almost all revenue comes from one drug, so a competing launch or a payer decision hits everything at once
$2.0B of debt against $588M of cash means more financing will be needed if sales disappoint
opportunities: Analysts see roughly 37% upside, with 20 of them covering the stock
Revenue went from $222M to $502M in a year and is running at $945M over the last twelve months: the launch is working
The same gene-targeted platform has several more programmes behind the first drug
watch: Quarterly Attruby prescriptions and how they compare with Pfizer's competing drug.
